---
title: "Quiz: neural networks"
---

Short questions on layers, the ReLU bend and training. Try each on paper first, then open the answer. A layer computes $\text{ReLU}(A\mathbf x + \mathbf b)$ with $\text{ReLU}(s) = \max(0, s)$ on each entry; training steps the weights against the gradient of a loss.

---

**Q1.** Compute $\text{ReLU}\big((2,\ -3,\ 0,\ 0.5)\big)$.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Entry by entry: negatives become 0, the rest pass through.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
$(2,\ 0,\ 0,\ 0.5)$.
:::

---

**Q2.** A colleague stacks ten layers, each a matrix plus a shift, with no ReLU in between. Can this network fit a curved intensity profile better than a single layer?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
What is $C(A\mathbf x + \mathbf b) + \mathbf d$?
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
No. $C(A\mathbf x + \mathbf b) + \mathbf d = (CA)\mathbf x + (C\mathbf b + \mathbf d)$: one matrix and one shift. However many layers, the result is a straight-line (linear) map. Only the bend between layers allows curves.
:::

---

**Q3.** A network with one input $x$ has three ReLU hidden units and one linear output. What does its output look like as a function of $x$?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Each hidden unit is $\max(0, a_k x + b_k)$.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
A continuous, **piecewise straight** line with at most three bends, one where each unit switches on ($x = -b_k/a_k$). Between the bends it is straight. More units allow more bends.
:::

---

**Q4.** You train with gradient descent and the loss jumps up and down and grows. What is the first thing to change?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
What controls the size of each step?
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
Lower the **learning rate** $\eta$. Steps that are too large overshoot the bottom of the valley and land higher on the other side; if each overshoot is larger than the last, the loss grows.
:::

---

**Q5.** How many numbers (weights and shifts) does a layer from a $28\times 28$ image to 64 hidden units have?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
The matrix is $64 \times 784$; one shift per hidden unit.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
$784 \cdot 64 + 64 = 50{,}240$.
:::

---

**Q6.** Why do neural networks for images need many training images?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Compare the number of weights with the number of examples.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
They have very many weights (hundreds of thousands). With few images, many different weight settings fit them equally well, including ones that just memorise the training images and fail on new ones. Many examples (or a penalty, or a smaller network) pin the weights down; checking on images not used for training shows whether it worked.
:::
